analysis.title: APAC Tech Views: SpaceX Q326 implications: Substantial capex upgrade to accelerate its build-out
key_insights: SpaceX Q326 sales grew 87% QoQ and 161% YoY to US$14.6bn, above the Street's US$12.9bn. Superintelligence (SI) was US$7.56bn (+195% QoQ), connectivity US$5.25bn (+29% QoQ) and space US$1.77bn (+104% QoQ). The share price rose 8% after hours.

Operating income swung from a net loss to a US$2.8bn gain. AI operating margin improved from -207% in Q325 and -49% in Q226 to positive 6% as cloud services ramp. Management called the quarter an inflection point.
Starlink subscribers grew from 12.0mn to 13.6mn. Monthly consumer ARPU rose 5% QoQ to US$69.

SI solutions/infrastructure revenue ramped from US$2.2bn to US$7.0bn (US$608mn from adding Cursor), with most of the rest from cloud. Backlog rose to US$63bn. ARR is projected to reach US$100bn by year-end (US$8.3bn monthly run rate) and US$500bn to US$1trn exiting 2027.
Management says cloud capex is paying back in under a year, in some cases 6 months, as compute stays tight and the value of a GW of compute rises with model intelligence.
Grok Bot agentic platform, launched in August, reached 800k paid weekly users. Grok Enterprise is above a US$1mn run rate (+50% QoQ).

Installed compute grew from 1.4GW to 1.7GW in Q326. The year-end target was raised from >2GW to 2.5-3GW. The 2027 target is to add a further 10GW and exit at 12.5-13GW, up from a prior 10GW, with a stretch target of adding 20GW.

SpaceX deploys mainly on NVIDIA. It installed 300MW in Q326 and targets about 1.3GW in Q426 (about 8.3k racks vs about 2k in Q3). For 2027 it expects to hold the pace at 200k per month while moving to NVIDIA's Vera platform.
UBS estimates 2.4mn Vera chips would be about 33k racks and 8.2GW. At US$8-9mn a rack that is US$260-300bn for compute and about US$350bn including networking and data center infrastructure.
Q3 capex was US$19.6bn vs US$18.1bn expected (US$16.4bn AI, US$1.5bn connectivity, US$1.6bn space). Q4 capex guidance is US$35-40bn vs prior Street US$19.8bn.
UBS (John Hodulik) raised SpaceX capex for 2026/2027 from US$56bn/US$124bn to US$73bn/US$310bn.
SpaceX exited Q3 with US$90bn cash and US$39bn debt. ROIC improved from -3.6% to 10.7%. It plans to keep its investment grade rating for debt financing.
UBS estimates 2027 operating cash flow grows from US$28bn to US$125bn, requiring US$170bn of financing cash flow and US$67bn from cash on hand.
Terafab targets initial production in H228 at its Texas site, with initial process based on Intel and talks with TSMC. UBS expects it to take several more years to become a major source.

Supply chain read: SpaceX's 33k Vera racks in 2027 would be 35% of UBS's 95k NVIDIA rack estimate. UBS CoWoS/HBM forecasts support up to 125k racks. Power is the key constraint, with UBS base case rising from 26GW to 51GW.
Super Micro rose 16% after hours after raising its Sep-quarter revenue outlook from US$14.5-15.5bn to US$18.5bn and gross margin from 10.4-10.8% to 12-12.5%.

Management expects weekly Starship flights in 1H27 and possibly twice-weekly in 2H27, up to 72 flights in 2027 (UBSe 30, Street 40). UBS sees WIN Semi's LEO revenue growing from 10% of sales in 2026 to 30% by 2028.

market_movers.rationale: Stronger Q3 results, raised compute and capex targets and a payback under a year on cloud capex. Shares rose 8% after hours from US$147.79.
Shares rose 16% after hours on a Sep-quarter revenue upgrade to US$18.5bn and gross margin guidance of 12-12.5%. Price US$32.46 on 20 Oct.
Key beneficiary of Starship flights and Starlink LEO build. UBS expects LEO revenue to rise from 10% of sales in 2026 to 30% by 2028 and gross margin to rise from 29% to over 37% by 2028.
SpaceX's commitment to NVIDIA Blackwell and Rubin/Vera racks implies upside to UBS's 95k rack estimate.
Primary foundry for the NVIDIA-related chain that SpaceX deployment supports.
Named as a primary memory supplier to the NVIDIA chain, alongside Samsung and SK Hynix.
Listed in disclosures as rated Buy. SpaceX may bring up competing AI accelerators on Terafab.

sector_views.rationale: SpaceX's capex raise and fast compute payback should lift AI supply chain sentiment and rack deployments, and ease worries about returns on AI investment.

earnings_insights: SpaceX Q3 2026 (reported 10/20 after the close): sales US$14.6bn actual vs US$12.9bn Street estimate. Q3 capex US$19.6bn actual vs US$18.1bn expected. Operating income was a US$2.8bn gain, versus a net loss in the prior period.
SpaceX Q4 capex guidance of US$35-40bn compares with prior Street estimate of US$19.8bn.
Super Micro raised its Sep-quarter revenue outlook from US$14.5-15.5bn to US$18.5bn and gross margin from 10.4-10.8% to 12-12.5%, a preannouncement not a final print.
risk_factors: Power supply is the key constraint on the compute build-out. UBS base case rises from 26GW to 51GW (57GW including general server).
Neo Clouds need to raise pricing on new contracts, find new capital including from chip companies, or cut lower-return projects.
SpaceX capex rises sharply while cash flow lags. 2027 needs US$170bn of financing cash flow and US$67bn from cash on hand.
Terafab execution and disruption risk in advanced semiconductor manufacturing, with a H228 initial production target.
vol_and_positioning: Investor feedback cited by UBS shows concern about returns on AI investment given rising capex relative to cash flows and uncertain monetization.

tension_points.bull_case: SpaceX reports cloud capex payback under a year, constrained compute and rising value of compute, which UBS says should lift AI supply chain sentiment.
tension_points.bear_case: Investors worry about returns on AI investment given rising capex relative to cash flows and uncertain monetization. SpaceX 2027 capex of US$310bn needs US$170bn of financing.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Neo Clouds failing to raise pricing on new contracts or source new capital, or upcoming cloud results lacking the better sales and margin trends.

theme_stances.key_argument: SpaceX's capex raise and fast payback on cloud deals support its aggressive expansion and lift the NVIDIA supply chain.
